questions.q: A hardware or software component that records every key pressed on a keyboard to steal passwords is called a:
questions.solution: Keyloggers capture keystrokes (often as spyware/trojan payloads), exposing passwords and OTPs. A sniffer passively captures network packets instead.
questions.shortcut: Key-strokes recorded = keylogger; network packets read = sniffer.

questions.q: Handouts printed with the '3 slides' layout are popular because:
options: Lines for audience notes appear beside each slide
They include the full speaker notes
questions.solution: The 3-slides-per-page handout prints each slide with ruled lines beside it so the audience can take notes. Speaker notes are NOT included (that is the Notes Pages layout).
questions.shortcut: 3-up = slides + note lines; Notes Pages = slide + your notes.

questions.q: Transistors were used as the basic technology of which generation of computers?
questions.solution: The 2nd generation (1956-63) replaced vacuum tubes with transistors, making computers smaller, faster and more reliable. 1st = vacuum tubes, 3rd = ICs, 4th = microprocessors.
questions.shortcut: Generation ladder: Vacuum -> Transistor -> IC -> Microprocessor -> AI. Transistor is the 2nd rung.

questions.q: Which chart type is best suited to show the trend of monthly sales over a year?
questions.solution: Line charts plot values across a continuous axis - ideal for time-series trends. Pie/doughnut show shares of one whole at a single point; radar compares multiple variables.
questions.shortcut: Trend over time = line, every time.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: The root **govern** keeps its n before -ment: government. Dropping the n is the single most common misspelling in this family.
questions.shortcut: Root n survives: govern + ment.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

A person appointed to hear both sides and settle a dispute
questions.solution: An **arbitrator** is the authorised settler of disputes. *Agitator* stirs trouble, *dictator* rules absolutely, *philanthropist* gives to charity — different families entirely.
questions.shortcut: Stem verb 'settle' → the deciding person-word.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Embarrass carries **double r and double s** — em-barr-ass. Each distractor drops exactly one of the doubles.
questions.shortcut: Double-double word: r and s both doubled.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The two leaders held detailed ___ on the border dispute.
questions.solution: 'Held detailed ___ on a dispute' asks for the discussion partnership: **deliberations**. The other options share the -tion shape but belong to wrong topics — parties celebrate, patients take medication, sound reverberates.
questions.shortcut: Governor-first: 'held detailed ___ on' → deliberations on.

questions.q: India finished at which position in the Commonwealth Games 2026 medal tally?
questions.solution: India stood 4th with 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze (39 medals), edging host Scotland (also 13 gold, 39 total) on the countback, behind Australia, and the top-2 medal nations.
questions.shortcut: Glasgow 2026: India 4th, 13-17-9 = 39.

questions.q: Which of Ashoka's **Major Rock Edicts** describes the Kalinga war and the king's remorse?
questions.solution: **Rock Edict XIII** records the conquest of Kalinga (c. 261 BCE), the deaths and deportations, Ashoka's repentance and his preference for *dhamma-vijaya*. RE II – medical care; RE V – Dhamma Mahamattas; RE XII – religious tolerance.
questions.shortcut: Unlucky **13** = war.

questions.q: The 18th BRICS Summit (2026) was held at —
questions.solution: India chaired BRICS in 2026 and hosted the 18th Summit on 12 September at **Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi**, with PM Modi, President Xi Jinping and President Putin among the leaders. Rio de Janeiro hosted 2025; Kazan 2024.
questions.shortcut: BRICS ladder: Kazan 2024 → Rio 2025 → New Delhi 2026.

questions.q: Keibul Lamjao, the only floating national park in the world, is home to which animal?
questions.solution: **Keibul Lamjao** on **Loktak Lake, Manipur** floats on *phumdis* and protects the endangered **Sangai** (brow-antlered deer). The hangul lives in Dachigam, the Nilgiri tahr in Eravikulam and the one-horned rhino in Kaziranga.
questions.shortcut: Animal-first list: Sangai → Keibul Lamjao.

questions.q: If $x=\dfrac{1}{2-\sqrt3}$, then the value of $x^3-2x^2-7x+5$ is:
questions.solution:
$x=\frac{1}{2-\sqrt3}=2+\sqrt3$, so $x-2=\sqrt3\Rightarrow x^2-4x+4=3\Rightarrow x^2-4x+1=0$.

Divide the cubic by $x^2-4x+1$: $x^3-2x^2-7x+5=(x^2-4x+1)(x+2)+3$.

Since $x^2-4x+1=0$, the value is $3$.
questions.shortcut: Form the quadratic $x^2-4x+1=0$ from the surd, then reduce: $x^3=4x^2-x$, so the expression $=4x^2-x-2x^2-7x+5=2x^2-8x+5=2(4x-1)-8x+5=3$.
questions.pattern: polynomial value at a conjugate surd

questions.q: A bag contains 50-paise, 25-paise and 10-paise coins in the ratio 7 : 6 : 5, amounting to ₹550 in all. The number of 25-paise coins is:
questions.solution:
Value of one set = 350 + 150 + 50 = 550 paise = ₹5.50.
Number of sets = 550 ÷ 5.50 = 100.
25-paise coins = 6 × 100 = **600**.
questions.shortcut: One set is worth ₹5.50; ₹550/5.50 = 100 sets ⇒ 600 twenty-five-paise coins.

questions.q: Two circles of radii $3$ cm and $8$ cm have their centres $13$ cm apart. The length of a transverse (cross) common tangent is:
questions.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 280 200" width="280" stroke="currentColor" fill="none"><circle cx="55" cy="100" r="18"/><circle cx="195" cy="100" r="48"/><line x1="55" y1="100" x2="195" y2="100" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/><line x1="55" y1="100" x2="55" y2="82"/><line x1="195" y1="100" x2="195" y2="52"/><text x="55" y="100" dx="-14" dy="8" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">O</text><text x="195" y="100" dx="0" dy="18" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">P</text><text x="55" y="82" dx="-12" dy="2" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">r</text><text x="195" y="52" dx="8" dy="2" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">R</text></svg>
questions.solution: Transverse tangent length $=\sqrt{d^2-(r_1+r_2)^2}=\sqrt{169-121}=\sqrt{48}=4\sqrt3$ cm.
questions.shortcut: $d=13$, $r_1+r_2=11$: $\sqrt{13^2-11^2}=\sqrt{48}=4\sqrt3$. Trap: $\sqrt{105}$ is the **direct** tangent $\sqrt{169-8^2}$. Both tangent types exist since $13>11$.

questions.q: A can do $\frac{2}{5}$ of a work in 6 days and B can do $\frac{3}{4}$ of the same work in 9 days. Working together, they complete the work in:
questions.solution:
A: full work in $\frac{6 \times 5}{2} = 15$ days; B: $\frac{9 \times 4}{3} = 12$ days.
Together: $\frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3}{20}$ ⇒ $6\frac{2}{3}$ days.
questions.shortcut: Scale each to full-work time first (15 and 12), then combine.

questions.q:
**Statement:** After the monsoon, a large number of potholes have appeared on the city's main road, causing long traffic jams every day.

**Conclusions:**
I. The municipal body should repair the potholes as early as possible.
II. All vehicles should be banned from the main road until the next monsoon.
III. Traffic police should be deployed on the road to manage the jams until the repairs are completed.

Which of the conclusions follow from the statement?
options: All of I, II and III follow
questions.solution: I fixes the root cause — **follows**. II is a disproportionate ban that paralyses the city and does not repair anything — **does not follow**. III is a sensible short-term relief while repairs go on — **follows**. Answer: **Only I and III**.
questions.shortcut: A permanent fix and a temporary relief can both be valid.

questions.q: Find the next term: **A3, D6, G9, J12, ?**
questions.solution: Letter track: A, D, G, J (+3) → M. Number track: 3, 6, 9, 12 (+3) → 15. Answer **M15**.
questions.shortcut: Two independent +3 columns; bolt the results together.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Song, Son, Sonar, Sone, Soon.** Which word comes **fourth**?
questions.solution: SON is a prefix of Sonar → Son first. Among SON- words compare the 4th letter: SONA (Sonar) < SONE (Sone) < SONG (Song). SOON splits at the 3rd letter (O > N), so it is last. Order: Son, Sonar, Sone, Song, Soon → fourth = **Song**.
questions.shortcut: Prefix first, then the 4th letter A < E < G; SOO- after all SON-.

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**10    6    64**

**12    4   128**

**9     5     ?**
questions.solution: 64 = 100 − 36 = 10² − 6²; confirm 128 = 144 − 16 = 12² − 4² ✓. Rule: third = a² − b². So 81 − 25 = **56**. (45 = 9×5 is the product trap; 70 and 85 come from slipping the squares.)
questions.shortcut: Both inputs squaring cleanly and a big third cell → a² − b².
questions.pattern: single grid, rows share a rule
